chunks: Say: "I am only a man like you, but it has been communicated to me that your Lord is one and single God, and that whosoever hopes to meet his Lord should do what is right, and not associate any one in the worship of his Lord."
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet being described as a man like us in this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the Prophet’s (SAWW) dual nature as both a human exemplar and a divinely inspired guide, reinforcing the concept of *Nubuwwah* (Prophethood) without attributing divinity to him. It serves as a foundational reminder for believers to align their *Amal* (deeds) with *Tawhid* (monotheism), ensuring that worship remains exclusive to Allah while anticipating the *Liqa’ Allah* (meeting with God). This instruction highlights the inseparable link between correct belief and righteous action in achieving spiritual proximity to the Divine.
